gen-gf-gabarito-gf-andika: Expressive from the first glance, Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib, its terminals cut open. Andika follows with sturdy tails and wide, easy turns on its s, which is the pair's steadiest quality.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-anta: Anta reads like bent wire, with gaping mouths on its e and a constant thickness throughout the line. Gabarito's open-cut terminals make it the livelier partner.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-antic: Gabarito looks drawn with one nib, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Antic uses that same nib-drawn habit, its letter mouths left open like an unjoined chalk arc, and that shared hand is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-ar-one-sans: Gabarito has no pinched joints or flared ends, just open-cut terminals that look drawn with one nib. AR One Sans lifts its brush ends away before each curve closes.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-assistant: Open-cut terminals give Gabarito a one-nib, hand-drawn look. It earns its keep big and short, where its unpinched curves can stretch out, while Assistant keeps its mouths open on c, e and a.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-asta-sans: Gabarito looks drawn with one nib, its terminals cut open. Asta Sans sits beside it in tubelike, constant-weight lines, and its e is never mistaken for a blot, so the page feels lively on top and approachable below.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-bai-jamjuree: Approachable and light, Bai Jamjuree has round, unpinched letters with no thick-and-thin modulation at all. Gabarito, drawn with one nib and open at the terminals, supplies the expressive edge above it.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-barlow: Barlow reads like neon tube, with constant strokes and c shapes whose tips are pulled well apart. Gabarito's open-cut one-nib look adds distinction.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-biz-udgothic: Expressive is the word for Gabarito, whose thin-looking letters have no thinner parts and terminals cut open. BIZ UDGothic opens a wide channel into every bowl, so a larger heading size would let the two stand apart nicely.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-biz-udpgothic: Gabarito has no pinched joints or flared ends, only open-cut terminals. BIZ UDPGothic spaces its letters lavishly, with a clear channel into each round shape, so a long passage would move along unhurried.
